language.script_notes: Buryat (also Cyrillic) appears around Lake Baikal and Ulan-Ude, and Tuvan around Kyzyl.

road_furniture.guardrail_type: Steel W-beam on the federal highway; long unprotected stretches elsewhere.
road_furniture.line_paint: Centre lines on the R254/R255 trans-Siberian highway and in towns; much of the network is unmarked or gravel.
road_furniture.curb_style: Painted kerbs in towns; unpaved edges common.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: White sign poles with a black base band. Wooden and concrete utility poles. The Trans-Siberian Railway and its power lines are frequently in view, and towns are strung along it with long empty gaps between.

architecture.roof_style: Flat Soviet block roofs in the cities; steep pitched roofs on wooden village houses to shed snow.
architecture.roof_material: Sheet metal, slate; painted metal on wooden houses.
architecture.wall_construction: A higher proportion of log and timber houses than European Russia, often unpainted and weathered grey; Soviet panel blocks in the regional capitals.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Weathered bare timber, faded blue and green paint, grey concrete.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Whole villages of log izby, sometimes on muddy unpaved streets; panel-block district centres; wooden Orthodox churches; the odd wooden watchtower or old ostrog remnant.

nature.vegetation: Endless taiga — larch, pine, spruce, birch — with larch turning bright gold in autumn; boggy forest across the flat West Siberian Plain; steppe and forest-steppe in the south toward Kazakhstan and Mongolia.
nature.terrain: The vast flat, waterlogged West Siberian Plain in the west; the higher Central Siberian Plateau; mountains around Baikal and toward Mongolia (Altai, Sayan, Khamar-Daban).
nature.climate_signature: The most extreme continental climate anywhere here — deep snow and hard light in winter, spring mud, short intense summers. A large share of the coverage is snow-covered or muddy.

vehicles.plate_color: White with a region number — codes in the 22s, 24s, 38s, 42s, 54s, 55s and 70s cover the main Siberian regions.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Ladas and UAZ off-roaders, plus a noticeable number of used Japanese cars filtering west from the Far East — but still mostly left-hand drive here, unlike the Far East proper.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Thin and linear — the trans-Siberian highway and railway corridor plus the big cities, with enormous unmapped gaps. Frequently deep snow.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Northern Kazakh forest-steppe and birch groves look almost identical; Cyrillic; Soviet blocks
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Kazakh plates and bilingual Kazakh/Russian (increasingly Latin) signage; Kazakhstan is more open and treeless as you go south.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country — Cyrillic, panelki, Russian plates, birch
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Siberia is emptier and rougher — more unpainted log houses, more larch, worse and often gravel roads, deeper snow, and the railway/power-line corridor always nearby.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Grassland, larch-clad mountains and Cyrillic near the southern border
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Mongolia has gers (yurts), far less paved road, Mongolian-style Cyrillic signage and Mongolian plates.
